title: Measurement-based characterization of spatial and depth-dependent activation in medical cyclotron vault concrete for decommissioning: The case study of the Severance Hospital
abstract: This study evaluated the spatial and depth-dependent activation characteristics of the concrete vault of a non-self-shielded IBA 18/9 Cyclone after a cooling period of approximately 3.5 years. A total of 520 concrete samples were systematically collected using a 1 m × 1 m grid-based sampling strategy with depth-resolved characterization up to 45 cm. Activation-related elemental compositions were analysed using ICP-MS and radionuclides were quantified using HPGe gamma spectrometry. The radionuclide inventory was dominated by 152 Eu and 60 Co, accounting for more than 85% of the total activity in most samples. Spatial distributions exhibited heterogeneous behaviour on wall surfaces, whereas the floor showed comparatively homogeneous activation characteristics. The highest activity levels were observed on the right wall where Targets 1 and 3 were intensively utilized during operation. Elevated activity values were identified above and below the target elevation. Most radioactivity was concentrated within the first 10–15 cm from the concrete surface. Exponential regression analyses showed attenuation coefficients of 0.047–0.055 cm −1 . The average activity decreased below the clearance level within the 25–30 cm depth interval. The present study provides a comprehensive measurement-based dataset and a quantitative framework that are directly applicable to decommissioning planning for regulatory release of activated cyclotron facilities.

Comprehensive Evaluation of γ-Ray Shielding in High-Density Glass Composites: Experimental Measurements and XCOM Validation
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the ability of glasses (A1-A5) possessing a range of densities (6.276 to 9.452 g/cm 3 ) to attenuate gamma radiation at three different photon energies. The study was conducted using a narrow-beam transmission method. Through determined several attenuation parameters such as transmission factors (TF), linear attenuation coefficients (μ), mass attenuation coefficients (μ/ρ), half value layers (HVL), and mean free path (MFP). The results were discovered that the TF for A1 at 1.332 MeV of incident photon energy and an initial thickness of 0.31 cm was approximately 0.91; indicating very little attenuation occurred at even higher photon energy. In contrast, reduced TF values for A1 measured at 0.662 MeV were between ∼0.80-0.85. The computed linear attenuation coefficient of A1 at 1.332 MeV is approximately 0.28-0.30 cm -1 . At 0.662 MeV, it is higher, ∼0.35 cm -1 . This causes the HVL values to increase between the values of approximately 2.0 cm at 0.662 MeV to approximately 2.4-2.6 cm at 1.332 MeV. Generally, the findings indicate that glass materials with high densities are more effective in getting rid of gamma rays, and thus good materials in terms of medical, industrial, and nuclear radiation protection.

title: Development of an Improved Reactivity Measurement System for Reactor Physics Tests during HANARO Startup
abstract: During the periodic reload startup physics tests of the HANARO research reactor, accurate evaluation of the critical control rod position and the shutdown margin is essential for operational safety. In this study, the legacy reactivity measurement system, which relied on a single compensated ionization chamber connected to an MS-DOS computer, was replaced with a modernized, multi-channel platform. The new system utilizes three spatially distributed fission chambers from the reactor regulation system to enhance measurement redundancy and robustness. Reactivity was evaluated using both the inverse kinetics equation and the least square inverse kinetics method to mitigate numerical drift under deep subcritical conditions. The developed system was validated during the 116th operation cycle of HANARO. In the approach-to-criticality test, the critical rod position was measured to be 180.4 mm. During the shut-off rod drop experiments, the multi-channel configuration effectively covered the localized spatial dependence associated with the detector geometry, confirming a conservative minimum shutdown margin of 11.182 $. The results demonstrate the practical applicability of the proposed multi-channel framework for supporting future startup physics tests and reactor operations.

title: Multi-phase and multi-species decomposition model for hydrogen peroxide in catalytic chambers
abstract: A mathematical model of the flow through a catalytic chamber to be used in rocket engines is presented. The model is based on a Lagrangian approach and a homogeneous description of the phases. The equation for the decomposition process is expanded to consider the pressure influence on the chemical reaction and the influence of the mass transfer effects (diffusion, adsorption and desorption). For the vaporization and the temperature determination the enthalpy is used. The pressure drop is calculated through a relation between the resistance coefficient and Reynolds number. Polynomial approaches are applied for the thermodynamic and transport properties. The heat transfer between the flow and the chamber wall as well as the flow and the catalytic material is considered. Finally, a comparison between the experimental test data and the simulation results is provided. The steady state values of temperature and pressure match the experimental data. The temperature data are in a range of 8 K, while the pressure data are in the uncertainty of the pressure sensors ( ± 1 bar). The transient behavior of the model shows a good agreement with the experimental data.

Lightweight design of an SNF disposal canister copper lid via topology optimization with stress linearization
abstract: The development of a Korean-type spent nuclear fuel (SNF) disposal canister based on the KBS-3 concept faces a challenge due to excessive copper consumption, as copper is a strategic material for corrosion resistance in deep geological environments. Since the lid accounts for a substantial portion of the copper used in the canister, a lightweight design is essential. However, ensuring structural integrity is challenging because stress singularities occur at sharp corners under handling loads. This study proposes a systematic two-step procedure combining density-based topology optimization and ASME Section VIII stress linearization to reduce the mass of the copper lid while ensuring structural safety. First, a baseline stress linearization was performed under a 3g lifting load to establish an allowable stress criterion independent of numerical singularities. Using this criterion as a post-optimization validation guide, lightweight candidate geometries were generated via compliance-minimization topology optimization and subsequently verified. As a result, the 48% material volume fraction model was selected as a suitable candidate design satisfying the allowable primary stress limits. This study presents a lightweight conceptual model that achieves a 52% reduction in copper mass under handling loads and suggests the potential for future implementation using metal additive manufacturing.

Temperature-dependent diffusion properties of three tropical wood species: Experimental measurements and numerical modeling
abstract: Wood is a hygroscopic material whose moisture transport behavior strongly influences dimensional stability, structural performance, and long-term durability in construction applications. Temperature also plays a crucial role in the diffusion process, as it alters the material properties and affects moisture migration mechanisms. Therefore, a thorough understanding of these coupled phenomena is essential for the reliable design and optimization of timber structural elements. In this context, the aim of this paper is to investigate the moisture diffusion properties of three tropical wood species, namely Ayous ( Triplochiton scleroxylon K. Schum.), Iatandza ( Albizia ferruginea Benth.), and Osanga ( Pteleopsis hylodendron Mildbr.) in different anisotropic planes and to evaluate the impact of heat treatments at 160 ∘ C and 200 ∘ C on these parameters. To this end, experiments were carried out using a low-cost diffusion setup under controlled hygrometric conditions, and moisture uptake data were analyzed using both an analytical approximation and an inverse numerical identification of Fick’s law. The results show strong hygroscopic anisotropy, with moisture diffusion occurring more rapidly along the longitudinal direction than in the radial-tangential plane. The diffusion coefficient generally increased with temperature, while the surface emission coefficient showed a more complex and less regular evolution depending on species, thickness, and thermal state. Among the investigated treatments, 160 ∘ C provides the best overall compromise for practical use, whereas 200 ∘ C leads to stronger modification of moisture transport behavior and a greater reduction in hygroscopicity. The results provide insight into the hygroscopic behavior of thermal-treated tropical woods and contribute to a better assessment of their dimensional stability and durability for timber construction applications.

Quadrature based dynamic event tree construction using FMU-driven piecewise deterministic Markov process for dynamic probabilistic risk assessment
abstract: Dynamic Probabilistic Risk Assessment (DPRA) methods are increasingly important to evaluate nuclear plant systems characterized by strong coupling between continuous physical dynamics, digital control logic, and stochastic component failures. Conventional sampling-based approaches, including Monte Carlo and next-event Piecewise Deterministic Markov Process (PDMP) methods, often require a prohibitive number of system simulations to resolve rare, time-dependent failure sequences. This work introduces a Quadrature based Dynamic Event Tree (QDET) framework that deterministically constructs weighted event-tree trajectories by discretizing hazard space rather than sampling failure times. The method preserves deterministic system evolution by coupling to a Functional Mock-up Unit (FMU) representation of the plant and control system and uses snapshot-based state restoration to avoid redundant simulations. The approach is formulated within a PDMP framework and enforces strict probability mass conservation while controlling combinatorial tree growth through quadrature, pruning, and cause ranking. The QDET method is validated against analytical solutions and Monte Carlo results using cold-standby and time-dependent K-out-of-N examples, demonstrating accurate probability estimation with orders-of-magnitude fewer system evaluations. The framework is further applied to the NRC Digital Feedwater Control System (DFWCS) benchmark under a realistic 24-hour power maneuver. The results show order-of-magnitude agreement with published benchmark failure probabilities and identify physically interpretable dominant risk contributors for both high- and low-level failure modes. These results demonstrate that QDET provides an efficient, deterministic, and scalable DPRA methodology suitable for high-fidelity digital control systems and advanced reactor applications.

STANDARDS Capability for Expedient Calculations of Used Nuclear Fuel Storage System and Transportation Package Dose Rates Using the On-the-Fly Shielding Analysis Method
abstract: The dose rates for used nuclear fuel storage systems and transportation packages are typically calculated using three-dimensional Monte Carlo (MC) computer codes such as Monte Carlo N-Particle (MCNP) or Standardized Computer Analyses for Licensing Evaluation (SCALE)/Monaco with Automated Variance Reduction using Importance Calculations (MAVRIC). As these are heavily shielded deep-penetration problems, the MC calculations require a significant number of particle histories to produce statistically acceptable estimates for the external dose rates. Even with the variance reduction techniques available with these programs, the runtimes for a single calculation often take days to achieve acceptably low statistical uncertainties. The “on-the-fly” method is being developed for the Storage, Transportation and Disposal Analysis Resource and Data System (STANDARDS) code system. It is named “on-the-fly” to describe how dose rate calculations can be performed quickly, reducing runtimes of days to just minutes. This is achieved by performing the MC calculations ahead of time on a per-particle and per-particle-energy basis for each axial burnup zone within each assembly location for many locations of interest around a specific spent nuclear fuel (SNF) storage system or transportation package design. Once the loading of a system or package is determined, the radiation source terms for gamma rays and neutrons emitted by the irradiated fuel, as well as for 60Co in the activated fuel assembly hardware, are calculated using the Transport Rigor Implemented with Time-dependent Operation for Neutronic depletion (TRITON)/Oak Ridge Isotope GENeration (ORIGEN) Assembly Isotopics (ORIGAMI) codes in the SCALE code system. The source term strength and spectra for each assembly are used with the on-the-fly libraries to quickly calculate the dose rate of the SNF storage system or transportation package. Although this method consists of a significant effort to generate libraries ahead of time, it results in the ability to save significant time when a specific system or loading pattern needs to be analyzed in the future. This paper presents the implementation of on-the-fly libraries into STANDARDS.

United States Nuclear Power Reactor Used Nuclear Fuel Database and Applications
abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy develops and maintains the Unified Database (UDB) within STANDARDS. The UDB serves as the foundational data infrastructure for managing the United States’ used nuclear fuel inventory of 329 237 discharged assemblies totaling 95 190 metric tons of heavy metal. The database organizes this inventory through approximately 200 interconnected tables. The schema is structured into eight primary attribute categories, supporting integrated analyses across storage, transportation, and disposal domains. Data enters the UDB through the GC-859 Nuclear Fuel Data Survey. The survey transitioned to web-based collection in 2023, improving data quality through real-time validation. The UDB enables automated generation of input files for nuclear analyses, reducing preparation time while maintaining traceability. Applications include national inventory reporting, Certificate of Compliance assessments, and facility optimization. The database distribution model balances accessibility with security requirements for federal agencies, national laboratories, and research organizations. The UDB provides essential data infrastructure as used fuel management transitions from site-specific to integrated national campaigns.

Fractional lagrangian modeling of non-Fickian radionuclide transport in heterogeneous geological media for Nuclear waste repository safety
abstract: The ability to accurately predict long-term radionuclide migration represents a key challenge for the safety assessment of the geological disposal of nuclear waste. The conventional transport models have successfully reproduced radionuclide migration in many repository studies. These models used the processes such as matrix diffusion, sorption, and fracture – matrix interactions. Anomalous transport behavior observed in some heterogeneous geological systems has motivated the exploration of alternative modeling frameworks. This study develops a fractional-order Lagrangian framework to examine the potential influence of sub-diffusion and super-diffusion on radionuclide plume evolution. The framework combines fractional advection-dispersion theory and particle-tracking modeling to yield mechanistic insights into Anomalous Transport. Example results show that memory effects lead to longer breakthrough curves, earlier arrivals than previously anticipated, and longer plumes tailing. Similarly, risk analysis showed that fractional dynamics also led to increased probabilities of exposure within the environment on longer time frames than classical models. Overall, the results indicate that memory effects in fractional dynamics lead to earlier radionuclide arrival times and longer tailing effects compared to classical behavior. As a result, environmental exposure is more probable over longer timescales. This study highlights that the safety assessment of deep geological repositories should account for memory effects. Adopting this approach is essential for creating a rational, defensible, and scientifically credible protection strategy to protect human health and the environment over the millennia following the disposal of nuclear waste. The presented approach offers a complementary framework for investigating anomalous transport behavior and memory effects that may not be explicitly represented in conventional formulations.

title: Radioisotope identification under spectral variability using convolutional neural network with structured 2-D transformed gamma spectra
abstract: : To achieve reliable radioisotope identification (RIID) under field-realistic spectral variability, we develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based RIID framework that reshapes one-dimensional (1-D) CsI(Tl) spectra into a structured two-dimensional (2-D) representation and applies 2-D convolutional structure to expand the effective receptive field and capture both local and global spectral correlations. Using experimentally measured single-isotope spectra, we synthesize 11,928 composite spectra across nine classes (eight RIs plus background), and augment for spectral variability via temperature-induced gain shifts (≈0–35 °C) and total-count ranges (1,000–200,000). We train paired models on 1-D versus reshaped 2-D inputs for multi-output regression of class contributions and evaluate them using mean squared error (MSE), mean magnitude of relative error (MMRE). Under these field-realistic conditions, the model trained on reshaped 2-D inputs (2-D model) outperforms its 1-D counterpart (1-D model), indicating not only higher identification accuracy but also enhanced robustness against spectral variability. Integrated Gradients analysis, validated by a model parameter randomization sanity check, confirms that both models rely on physically meaningful photopeaks; however, the 2-D model more systematically incorporates non-target spectral features as negative evidence against the target RI. Additional analyses demonstrate that the performance gain arises from both the two-dimensional input reshaping and the multi-directional convolutional operations that exploit it, enabling effective joint modeling of local spectral features and global inter-RI dependencies under the unity-sum constraint.

title: Net heat-flux measurement method for passive radiative cooling materials with ambient self-tracking
abstract: Passive Radiative Cooling (PRC) materials can efficiently dissipate thermal energy to outer space through the atmospheric window (8–14 µm), while reflecting most incident solar radiation, enabling sub-ambient cooling under direct sunlight. This work presents RAFT (Radiative Ambient-referenced Flux Testbed), a compact device for accurate outdoor PRC materials characterization. RAFT employs a heat flux meter to directly measure net heat flux, with the PRC sample mounted on the sensing surface and thermally coupled to an ambient-tracked reservoir via a compact fan-based convective heat exchanger integrated with heat pipes. Outdoor experiments demonstrated reliable ambient temperature tracking and accurate net heat flux measurements, which were further verified using an openly-released numerical model. Compared with conventional resistive heater-based outdoor setups, RAFT overcomes key limitations: it eliminates the need for feedback-control, shortens the measurement chain, reduces measurement noise when sample temperature approaches ambient, and enables quantification of both cooling and heating net fluxes with a total measurement uncertainty of ±1.8 W m -2 . Relative to liquid-flow-based systems, RAFT offers improved portability and avoids the complexities of fluid handling. The proposed setup provides a robust and practical framework for outdoor evaluation of PRC materials, addressing the current lack of standardized protocols for direct heat flux measurement.

Introducing FREDS: Fit Reactor Energy Discretization Search
abstract: We introduce FREDS, a multi-objective optimization Python framework for energy grid discretization in reactor neutronics calculations. FREDS uses sensitivity profiles derived from the Serpent2 Monte Carlo code to guide the allocation of energy groups, aiming to exploit the trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency. Multi-objective optimization is performed using genetic algorithms, allowing FREDS to optimize the energy grids for the keff sensitivity to multiple reactions simultaneously while minimizing the number of energy groups in the mesh. We demonstrate its capabilities on both fast and thermal benchmarks, namely Godiva, Jezebel, and UAM, optimizing the keff sensitivity to fission, capture, and elastic scattering reactions. We demonstrate the application of FREDS through the optimizations performed in this work, showing its effectiveness in generating accurate and computationally efficient discretizations across a variety of reactor systems and reactions of interest, in agreement with the underlying physics.

title: A Review of Primary Activity Measurement Based on β-γ Coincidence Counting
abstract: Over the past several decades, the β-γ coincidence counting method has been well established as a primary technique for radionuclide standardization. This review introduces the fundamental principles of β-γ coincidence counting and outlines the various techniques employed in primary activity measurement based on β-γ coincidence methods, supported by an extensive bibliography of current research in the field. The literature is summarized with respect to detector types, β-γ detector configurations, data acquisition system designs, and efficiency extrapolation techniques, followed by representative, summarized validation results reported across various implementations. A concise overview of the practical advantages and limitations associated with these methodologies is also included, and opportunities for future research are subsequently highlighted.

Corrosion behaviour of U-bend 316 stainless steel in static liquid lead at 550 and 700°C
abstract: The compatibility of material structural with liquid lead (Pb) is a critical factor for the longevity of high-temperature nuclear systems. The corrosion behaviour and mechanism of 316 stainless steel (316SS) U-bend specimens subjected to 150-hour static immersion tests at 550°C and 700°C, respectively. This study systematically investigates the local corrosion behaviour of U-bend 316SS specimens under high-temperature liquid Pb exposure, representing realistic stress conditions experienced by U-tube heat exchanger structures in the coolant circulation circuit of LFR. The results shows oxidation was identified as the primary degradation mode at 550°C, leading to the development of a characteristic duplex scale composed of an outer Fe-O layer and an inner Fe-Cr spinel. However, at 700°C, a transition to dissolution corrosion occurred, driven by the increased solubility of Ni, Cr, and Fe in liquid Pb. Dissolution corrosion causes thinning of the specimen at a temperature of 700°C. The oxygen saturation limit in liquid Pb corresponds to solubilities of 1.27 × 10−3 wt% and 1.11 × 10−2 wt% at 550°C and 700°C, respectively. At 550°C, oxygen availability is insufficient for the development of a continuous protective Cr-oxide scale, leading to negligible oxidation. At 700°C, however, the markedly higher oxygen solubility promotes the formation of an Fe-Cr-O oxide system. Then, the impact of height reduction variations (0.9 cm and 1.0 cm) indicating that minor differences in local strain do not significantly exacerbate the corrosive attack. This indicates that the variation in deformation was insufficient to substantially alter Pb diffusion pathways.

Thermomechanical Analysis of UO2 Fuel Rods with SiC_f/SiC Composite Cladding under Normal and Accident Conditions
abstract: To assess the mechanical response and structural integrity of fuel cladding under high-temperature conditions, a two-dimensional axisymmetric finite-element model of a UO 2 –SiC composite cladding system was developed. The model incorporates key fuel performance mechanisms including irradiation swelling, high-temperature creep, and fission gas release. Applicability was verified by mesh-independence studies and comparison with published data. Simulations covered steady-state operation with linear heat rates from 18 to 26 kW/m and LOCA scenarios with coolant injection delays of 50–90 s. At the upper bound steady state (26 kW/m), fission gas release produced a nonlinear rise in plenum pressure up to 32 MPa, which became the dominant contributor to cladding hoop stress. Under LOCA conditions, peak stress strongly depends on coolant injection timing; however, effective cooling within a 100 s window limited peak stress below 100 MPa, indicating a manageable failure risk. Weibull-based failure analysis yields probabilities below 1.2×10 -5 for steady-state operation at the maximum linear heat rate of 26 kW/m, and below 9.5×10 -12 for accident scenarios initiated from a steady-state power of 18 kW/m. These results demonstrate the model’s utility as a practical tool for evaluating the mechanical behavior of advanced cladding systems under both normal operation and accident scenarios.

title: Efficient Multi-Parameter Optimization Design of Cyclotron-Based Compact Thermal Neutron Radiography System
Monte Carlo Neutronic Analysis of Er2O3 Discrete Burnable Absorber Rods in a VVER-1200 Fuel Assembly
abstract: Er 2 O 3 discrete burnable absorber rods in a TVSA-12-type VVER-1200 hexagonal fuel assembly were evaluated using OpenMC with the ENDF/B-VIII.0 nuclear data library. Nine configurations were investigated, comprising Er 2 O 3 concentrations of 2–8 wt% in 12 ring-5 rods, rod-count variants of 6–18 rods at 4 wt%, and Gd 2 O 3 reference cases. Beginning-of-life reactivity worth ranged from −1,116 to −2,945 pcm, while the reactivity efficiency decreased from −558 to −368 pcm/wt%. Rod-count scaling was linear (−149.3 pcm/rod; R 2 = 0.9993), indicating negligible inter-rod self-shielding. Depletion to 60 MWd/kgU produced a monotonic decline in k ∞ for all Er 2 O 3 cases, in contrast to a +129 pcm mid-cycle reactivity recovery for the 4 wt% Gd 2 O 3 case. Approximately 97% of the initial Er-167 inventory was depleted by the end of the cycle under the adopted depletion model. Doppler temperature coefficients remained negative, ranging from −1.9 to −3.5 pcm/K over the burnup range, while moderator temperature coefficients remained negative throughout. Multi-criteria decision analysis identified the 4 wt% Er 2 O 3 , 12-rod configuration as the engineering optimum, providing −1,822 pcm reactivity suppression, a 192 ppm (7.1%) reduction in critical boron concentration, an assembly-level radial power peaking factor (K q ) of 1.514, and a burnup penalty of only 0.4 MWd/kgU.

title: Monte Carlo–Based Operational Robustness of JE01-BC01 Heat Exchanger Using State Space Deviation
abstract: Operational uncertainty affects the thermal–hydraulic performance of the JE01-BC01 shell-and-tube heat exchanger in the RSG-GAS research reactor, a safety-critical cooling component. This study proposes a state-space–based robustness framework that integrates Monte Carlo simulation with a State Space Deviation (SSD) metric to quantify multivariate operational deviations under stochastic variations in cooling-water mass flow rate, inlet temperature, and pressure drop. Results show that, despite nominal compliance (NTU 0 = 2.78), operational variability produces a wide state dispersion (SSD = 0–0.2029) and reduces NTU to 2.63, indicating degraded margins. Performance degradation is evaluated using an effectiveness threshold (ε < 0.70), where several states approach this limit, revealing latent vulnerabilities not captured by deterministic analysis. The weak correlation between the performance index and SSD (r = 0.17) further indicates that thermal performance alone is insufficient to characterize operational robustness. The SSD framework links multivariate operational deviations to maintenance relevance and enables identification of fragile operating regimes. Although neglecting fouling and parameter uncertainty may slightly overestimate performance, overall trends remain consistent. SSD provides a physically interpretable, state-space–based robustness metric that captures multivariate operational deviations not fully represented by conventional indicators such as NTU and effectiveness, enabling a clearer distinction between thermal performance and operational robustness.

abstract: Pressurized heavy water reactors (PHWRs) fueled with natural uranium (NU) are constrained by low discharge burnup (∼7500 MWd/MTHM), high spent fuel volumes, and a positive coolant void reactivity (CVR) that poses a safety challenge under loss-of-coolant accident (LOCA) conditions. Clean Core Thorium Energy, Inc. (CCTE) is developing Advanced Nuclear Energy for Enriched Life (ANEEL), a thoria-urania (ThO₂-UO₂) mixed oxide fuel using high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) and a burnable neutron absorber, designed as a “plug and play” replacement for existing PHWR NU fuel bundles. This paper presents physics, thermal-hydraulic, and fuel performance analyses supporting the technical feasibility of ANEEL fuel in a CANDU-6 reactor. Fuel composition optimization using DRAGON/DONJON yielded a design achieving an average discharge burnup of over 44,000 MWd/MTHM — approximately six times that of NU fuel — while reducing the full-core CVR from 16.4 mk to below 13.3 mk for an equilibrium core. Core-follow simulations confirm that maximum channel and bundle powers remain within licensing limits throughout the fresh-to-equilibrium transition. Independent MCNP calculations confirm that reactivity device worths deviate by no more than 16% from NU values and that the fuel and moderator temperature coefficients are more negative for ANEEL compared to NU fuel. CATHENA LOCA simulations show peak sheath and centerline temperatures for ANEEL are lower than for NU fuel. PEGASUS finite element analysis confirms structural integrity throughout irradiation, with fission gas pressure remaining below coolant pressure and end-of-life cladding strain of much less than 1%. These results demonstrate that ANEEL fuel achieves substantially higher burnup with improved safety margins relative to NU fuel, with manageable impacts on existing PHWR core design and control systems.

This study mainly investigates the identification method of important non-safety level Structure, System, and Components (SSCs) for passive advanced light water reactor type from Probabilistic Safety Analysis theory. Based on the actual case of the Advanced Hualong Pressurized Reactor 1000, a systematic study was conducted using the Probabilistic Safety Analysis model in the aspects of accident mitigation and uncertainty analysis. Important non-safety SSCs were identified in the Advanced Hualong Pressurized Reactor 1000, providing a valuable reference for subsequent engineering applications. It also provided strong technical support for the optimization of regulatory requirements for non-safety level systems of passive advanced light water reactors.

Physics-Based Conjugate Heat Transfer Refinement for Microlayer Sub-Grid Model and X-ray-Informed Transition-Angle Modeling for Single-Bubble Nucleate Boiling Simulations
abstract: Accurate prediction of nucleate boiling heat transfer remains challenging due to the multiscale interactions among microlayer evaporation, conjugate heat transfer, and near-wall interfacial dynamics. In the present study, a physics-based and computationally efficient conjugate heat transfer refinement for the microlayer subgrid model is developed to simulate single-bubble nucleate boiling. A transition-angle concept, derived from synchrotron X-ray imaging, is introduced to reconstruct the transition region between the microlayer and the bulk liquid beneath a growing bubble. The model is implemented within a CLSVOF framework and validated against X-ray experimental data. The results show that the transition-angle model improves predictions of bubble growth and transition-region geometry compared with simulations based on the apparent contact angle. Energy balance analysis confirms that the model accurately captures the coupling between wall heat transfer and microlayer evaporation. Heat-transfer analysis demonstrates that the microlayer, transition, and bulk regions contribute approximately 55%, 20%, and 25% of the total bubble heat transfer, respectively, under the wall superheat condition of 20K. The predicted transition-region contribution agrees closely with experimental measurements, whereas conventional simulations based on the apparent contact angle will significantly underestimate it. The proposed approach provides a more physically consistent framework for predicting the partitioning of wall heat transfer in nucleate boiling.

title: Correlation-informed neural networks for predicting flow boiling heat transfer coefficient in mini/micro-channels
abstract: In this study, we develop a correlation-informed neural networks (CINNs) framework for predicting flow boiling heat transfer coefficients (HTC) in mini/micro-channels, addressing key limitations of purely data-driven artificial neural networks (ANNs) models and traditional empirical correlations. The proposed framework integrates consolidated experimental data with an established universal correlation through a physics-informed loss function, enabling the model to leverage both data-driven flexibility learning and physically grounded constraints. A comprehensive database of around 17,000 data points, along with four representative universal correlations, is used to train and evaluate the CINNs model. A physics-weighting parameter is introduced to modulate the balance between measured data and embedded physical knowledge. Model evaluations demonstrate that the CINNs framework achieves markedly improved prediction accuracy relative to standalone empirical correlations and exhibits enhanced robustness compared to the purely data-driven ANNs model, particularly when the training dataset is limited. Uncertainty quantification analyses further reveal the sensitivity of the CINNs performance to the underlying physics model and the amount of available training data. In addition, tests on unseen fluids show that the CINNs model provides substantially better extrapolation capability than the ANNs model, highlighting the benefits of incorporating physics-based structure into the learning process. Finally, the CINNs framework is leveraged to refine an existing correlation (Kim and Mudawar) by learning consistent parameter adjustments, yielding an ≈ 4% improvement in predictive accuracy. Taken together, these results demonstrate that the CINNs framework offers a powerful and data-efficient approach for modeling flow boiling heat transfer in compact channels, providing a significant advancement over conventional methods.

Reconstruction of temperature and heat flux from Thermal Large Eddy Simulations using Deep Learning
abstract: It is paramount to understand the coupling between velocity and temperature for many flows found in nature, or industrial applications, like in solar receivers, found inside concentrated solar power towers. Thermal-Large Eddy Simulation (T-LES) is a set of turbulence and thermal modeling equations for turbulent flows with an important thermal component.T-LES modeling can capture the largest scales of turbulence and heat flux fluctuations at a reasonable cost compared to DNS. However, fluctuations at small scales are not captured.This study develops and compares three different methods to reconstruct the small scales of temperature fluctuations by inverting the numerical T-LES filter. This filter is never fully known. First, a supervised learning method only applicable \textit{a priori}. Second, a weakly supervised learning method, requiring the two point correlation of the temperature. This method is applicable \textit{a posteriori}. A third method is proposed based on the Adaptive Local Deconvolution Method applied in a constrained learning framework with a single filter.The results of the first method highlight the ability of the neural network to generalize the filter inversion from a small number of training examples, on both the temperature fields and on the reconstructed heat flux. The results of the second method show the capability of the network to reconstruct plausible raw data and to fit the statistics of the Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) on temperature fields. The third method exhibits satisfactory results while involving only a few parameters to learn on temperature and heat flux.

abstract: For the first time, Li 2 CaSiO 4 :Eu 2+ single crystalline scintillation material has been grown and evaluated for the scintillation properties. Samples are grown by high temperature solution-melt method; a mixture of LiF–LiCl is used as a solvent. Density of the material is measured to be 2.55 g/cm 3 . Samples demonstrate light output under neutron irradiation of 25000 ph/neutron, which is 4.3 times higher than commercial Ce-doped lithium glass GS20. Its effective scintillation decay constant is estimated to be 180 ns. These findings demonstrate that the obtained combination of the scintillation parameters, even for the first samples, makes the material highly promising for thermal neutron measurement and monitoring in the nuclear power industry.

title: Integration scenario of a distributed Traveling Wave Antenna in European DEMO
abstract: A preliminary engineering feasibility study of the integration of a Traveling Wave Antenna (TWA) in European DEMO is presented. Unlike conventional ICRF antennas in vacuum vessel ports, the TWA is embedded in blanket segments, avoiding the dimensional constraints imposed by such ports. Thus, a substantial increase in the antenna surface area can be achieved, thereby reducing the surface power density. This is particularly important for larger machines like DEMO, where higher power levels are needed for plasma heating. This work presents initial assessments of how this integration affects tritium breeding, thermo-hydraulic performance, and remote-handling compatibility of the blanket. The analysis indicated a reduction in the blanket’s tritium breeding ratio by only 2%. Thermo-hydraulic analysis indicated that the maximum temperatures obtained remain below 550 ° C for a Eurofer based antenna, and the pressure drop in the antenna cooling circuit generally remains below 5 kPa. The structural checks of the antenna straps indicated compliance with the RCC-MRx design rules for monotonic damage modes under standard operating loads. The compatibility of the antenna with remote handling of the blanket segment was assessed and no fundamental incompatibility was identified for the present configuration. This early screening-level study aims to pave the way for further engineering refinement of the integration of TWA in DEMO.

title: A design and experimental investigation of thermal characterization of a high-power lithium target under proton-beam-equivalent loading for accelerator-based boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT)
abstract: In this study, the thermal management of a high-power lithium target utilized in accelerator-based boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is systematically investigated through numerical simulations and experimental validation. A modular-designed thermal experimental platform is developed, capable of operating under a wide range of flow rates, temperatures, and cooling capacities, ensuring precise control and repeatability for high-power target characterization. A 15.8 kW prototype target with a unit heat flux density of 1.58 MW/m 2 is constructed, employing microchannel-cooled copper substrates and electric heating rods to simulate proton beam heat deposition; the beam effect is represented by a beam-equivalent thermal load. Three microchannel configurations were evaluated using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models coupled with the SST k-ω turbulence model, validated against experimental data for Reynolds numbers spanning 560–18,700. The optimized 1 mm microchannel design demonstrated superior thermal performance, achieving 93.2% heat removal efficiency at 3.6 m/s coolant velocity while maintaining 28% lower pressure drop compared to conventional designs. Transient analysis of pulsed proton beam operation revealed attenuated temperature fluctuations in the lithium layer, attributable to efficient substrate cooling and thermal buffering by the anti-blistering layer. The numerical model is established in accordance with the thermal mock-up configuration, and the experimental measurements show good agreement with the CFD predictions, confirming the reliability of the proposed thermal management strategy. These findings establish a validated framework for thermal characterization of high-power BNCT targets, providing essential design guidelines and operational insights for managing extreme thermal loads in next generation neutron sources.

Enhanced Thermal Management via Phase Change Energy Storage Radiator a Numerical Study
abstract: Based on the enthalpy-porosity model, this study establishes a numerical framework for simulating phase change material (PCM) melting and solidification in a thermal energy storage radiator, addressing increased thermal dissipation demands from high-performance electronic devices. The influence of PCM melting temperature on heat storage performance under transient heat flux is examined, along with heat storage/release characteristics under periodic high/low heat flux and pulsed intermittent heating. Results indicate that the PCM radiator effectively mitigates initial thermal shocks and substantially extends the safe operational time of the heat source. Under exponentially increasing heat flux, the thermal buffering capacity is highly dependent on matching the PCM melting temperature with the transient thermal load to maximize latent heat utilization. Furthermore, under periodic and pulsed intermittent heating, increasing the cycle frequency significantly enhances the overall cooling performance. Higher frequencies prevent severe thermal accumulation and lower the peak heat source temperature, as the shortened heating intervals and subsequent off-periods allow for effective heat dissipation and partial PCM solidification recovery. Overall, this study provides generalized guidelines for optimizing PCM-based heat sinks under complex, highly transient thermal loads.

title: Temperature Separation and Flow Analysis in an Annular Vortex Tube
abstract: Energy separation between co-axial swirling flows is a common phenomenon in counter-flow vortex tube. In this study, the energy analysis involving the terms of work and heat transfers is carried out with a help of a separator tube to verify the cooling process inside the vortex tube. The separator tube forms a novel part of this work, which gives a hint in verifying the theories of heat transfer and shear viscous work across the core and peripheral flow layers. The energy separation or Ranque-Hilsch effect is verified for different materials of separator tube, while the tube length remains constant across all operating conditions. Heat transfer by turbulent convection and shear work term are reported to understand the significance of contribution to energy separation. Separator tube suppresses the tangential work transfer from 130 W to 14 W, where almost 9/10 of the net energy transfer is decreased. It is found that 58% reduction in temperature separation with separator tube. This effect is increased to 77% and 90% with aluminum and poly vinyl chloride materials as separator tubes. It is found that predominant effect of temperature separation arises from tangential work transfer as compared to axial shear work and heat transfer.

title: An Asymptotic Solution for Thermal Response in Biological Tissue Induced by Pulsed Laser Based on Dual-Phase-Lag Model
abstract: This study presents an asymptotic solution for predicting the thermal response in biological tissues subjected to pulsed laser irradiation using the dual-phase-lag bio-heat transfer model. By applying the Laplace transform coupled with the initial-value theorem, a simplified time-domain solution is derived that effectively captures non-Fourier thermal behavior and clearly reveals qualitative relationships between key parameters and the thermal response. Results show that the ratio of phase lag times critically influences the thermal profile, with smaller values of the ratio of phase lag times reducing peak temperature and enhancing heat uniformity. Furthermore, for constant total energy input, higher-power and shorter-pulse laser configurations induce greater peak temperatures and more extensive thermal damage near the tissue surface. These findings provide theoretical insight into laser-tissue interactions and offer practical guidance for optimizing clinical laser procedures toward minimally invasive and energy-efficient treatments.

title: Variable Properties in Fouling Estimation in Heat Exchanger Networks with Fouling
abstract: Fouling in shell-and-tube heat exchangers reduces heat recovery efficiency in industrial processes, increasing fuel consumption and operational costs. Most studies assume constant physical properties throughout the heat exchanger network (HEN) and over time, despite the impact of temperature-dependent properties on heat transfer and fouling behavior. This work proposes a variable-property framework for HEN simulation with fouling, assuming pseudo-stationary fouling behavior within each time step. Physical properties are updated through a direct substitution approach based on estimated temperatures, with iterative convergence. Temperature-dependent effects on mixing and furnace duty are also incorporated. Results indicate that the proposed approach predicts lower initial fouling rates and outlet temperatures. However, over time, reduced fouling leads to higher predicted outlet temperatures compared to the constant-property approach. Overall, the variable-property model results in a 14.4% increase in estimated operational costs, indicating that constant-property models may underestimate true operating costs. Convergence is achieved in approximately three iterations on average, indicating a favorable tradeoff between improved model fidelity and computational effort.

Retirement or Renewal? Decision-making processes for long-term operations of nuclear power plants
abstract: A large share of the world's nuclear fleet now operates near or beyond its original design lifetime, calling for making decisions about entering long-term operation (LTO). Remarkably, Nuclear Power Plants (NPPs) that face comparable technical and regulatory conditions often arrive at different outcomes: some enter LTO, while others are permanently shut down. Against this background, we formulated our research question: What are the factors shaping the decision-making process for NPP LTO? We addressed this gap through open interviews with senior utility and vendor leaders in the U.S. context, analyzed via the Gioia method and triangulated with relevant public documents. We identified several promoting and hindering factors for the LTO decision-making process overlooked in the literature, showing their different impact in regulated and deregulated markets. In particular, license renewal (LR) is routinely treated as a real option - a low-cost right rather than an obligation - used to reduce uncertainty while postponing life extension (LE) capital investments until revenue conditions are clearer. Indeed, LE costs are quite predictable while revenues remain uncertain and are fundamentally shaped by market design. Plants in U.S. deregulated markets face uncertain wholesale price cycles and policies, with pressures newly tempered by premium power purchase agreements from data center/AI loads and federal-state incentives in some cases. Human resources create delivery risk due to a lack of skilled workers, especially in temporary endeavours for LE projects. Of note, ageing management plays a key role from a techno-economic perspective, since it evolved from compliance to strategy, creating synergies with LE programs and power uprates. This article provides an option-based view of LR, identifies market design as a first-order moderator of LTO economics, and offers actionable guidance on timing, financing, workforce, and stakeholder engagement.

Gamma-Ray Shielding Performance of Ho 2 O 3 –Doped Borate Glasses: Influence of ZnO and CaO Substitution
abstract: Lead-free transparent materials that effectively attenuate gamma radiation as alternatives to traditional shielding are being explored in medical, industrial, and nuclear sectors; there is increasing interest in using new materials. There are a variety of studies available on the performance of borate glasses for radiation shielding that have explored the addition of various rare earth elements and different network modifiers to achieve radiation attenuation. However, no comprehensive study has been done on how to use both zinc oxide (ZnO) and calcium oxide (CaO) as co-substituents for holmium oxide (Ho2O3)–doped borate glass in order to improve gamma-ray attenuation properties.To fill this gap in knowledge, four different glass compositions made from a system of B2O3, Na2O, ZnO, CaO, and Ho2O3 were produced using traditional melt-quenching methods. The density of each glass sample was measured using the Archimedes method. The gamma-ray attenuation properties of the samples were evaluated using a NaI(Tl) scintillation detector and standard radioactive sources (241Am, 137Cs, and 60Co), with gamma-ray photon energies ranging between 0.059 MeV and 1.332 MeV.The experimental linear attenuation coefficients (LAC) were compared to the theoretical LACs calculated with Phy-X/PSD. Additional shielding properties, such as the half-value layer (HVL), mean free path (MFP), tenth-value layer (TVL), transmission factor (TF in percent), and radiation shielding efficiency (RSE in percent), were also evaluated.The fabricated glass density increased from 2.98 to 3.29 g/cm3 as the composition was modified gradually through the series. The experimental LAC measurements supported the theoretical values with only a few percent difference between the two (software showing < 6% deviation). The highest attenuation of all the samples was exhibited by Zn20Ho1 with LAC values of 3.531 cm−1 at 0.059 MeV and 0.169 cm−1 at 1.332 MeV and also the lowest HVL, MFP, and TVL values. The results for TF and RSE further supported the excellent shielding of the higher density compositions throughout this energy range.When compared to previously studied glass and concrete shielding materials, the fabricated glasses had competitive mass attenuation coefficients. The enhancement of the observed shielded materials can be attributed to the modification of the material composition, resulting in changes to the ZnO and CaO contents and density simultaneously. Therefore, the investigated glasses containing Ho2O3 show good promise as gamma-ray attenuating materials and present an exciting new environmentally friendly shielding option for use in protecting against radiation.

The Effect of MgO, CaO, and SrO on the Optical Properties and Radiation Attenuation Behavior of Sb 2 O 3 -Li 2 O-Er 2 O 3 Glasses: A Theoretical Study
abstract: The effect of MgO, CaO, and SrO on the optical properties and radiation attenuation behavior of Sb2O3-Li2O-Er2O3 (SLE) glasses has been theoretically investigated. Glasses including Mg were labeled SLEMg, those including Ca were labeled SLECa and those including Sr were labeled SLESr. The molar refractivity and molar polarizability of SLEx glasses are in the order SLEMg < SLESr < SLECa. The SLESr has slightly higher reflection loss but slightly lower optical transmission than SLEMg and SLECa. The static dielectric constant and optical dielectric constant are slightly higher for SLESr than for SLEMg and SLECa and slightly lower for SLEMg than for SLESr and SLECa. At 10 -MeV energy, SLESr has a slightly higher linear attenuation coefficient and mass attenuation coefficient than SLEMg and SLECa, whereas it has slightly lower half-value layer, tenth-value layer, and mean free path than those of SLEMg and SLECa. The effective atomic number (Zeff) of SLESr is slightly higher, and the Zeff of SLEMg is slightly lower, between 1 and 15 MeV, than those of the other studied glasses. However, the effective electron density (Neff) of SLESr glass is slightly lower, and the Neff of SLEMg is slightly higher, between 5 and 15 MeV, than those of the other studied glasses. The equivalent atomic numbers of SLESr are slightly higher than those of the other glasses, between 2 and 15 MeV. Consequently, SLESr has slightly better radiation attenuation properties.

Legal investigation on final disposal for no HLW generation nuclear fuel cycle option
abstract: This study evaluates the legal compliance of a nuclear fuel cycle option designed to eliminate the generation of high-level radioactive waste (HLW). Building upon previous research on total waste volume control – which proposed a fuel cycle utilizing 90Sr and 137Cs transmutation to avoid HLW generation – this paper examines how these specific waste streams align with existing legal frameworks. Specifically, the waste streams are analyzed and classified under both the Final Disposal Act and the Reactors Regulation Act. The analysis has identified three novel waste forms generated by this fuel cycle, which currently fall under low-level waste (LLW) and clearance waste classifications. Based on these findings, we recommend specific revisions to the Final Disposal Act to clarify the legal compliance or suitability and resolve classification ambiguities for these new waste streams. Ultimately, this legal assessment, combined with the technical fuel cycle design, provides a necessary framework for evaluating public acceptance of nuclear fuel cycle options.

title: Investigating the Neutronic Potential of Control Rod Materials for Improved Accident Tolerance and Providing Sufficient Shutdown Margin in PWRs under Uprated Conditions
abstract: In this study, the neutronic performance of high worth control rods is evaluated. Firstly, the control rod worth of absorber materials including Dy 2 O 3 , Eu 2 O 3 , Gd 2 O 3 , Hf, HfB 2 , HfO 2 , Ho 2 O 3 , and Sm 2 O 3 in a PWR assembly model as a function of control rod degradation fuel, with comparison to conventional B 4 C and Ag-In-Cd. Use of high worth claddings for the control rods was also considered, specifically Hf and TZM. For selected materials, whole core shutdown margin analysis was also performed for a typical PWR. A core with 20% uprate and LEU+ fuel was investigated and compared to a conventional LEU-fueled core, to quantify the erosion of SDM with higher enrichment and increased power defect and the potential of the high worth control rod materials to mitigate this. Eu 2 O 3 was also found to be a potential option for a soluble boron free core due to retaining its worth with irradiation, although post-shutdown decay could present challenges. At the end of cycle of the 20% uprated core, only Eu 2 O 3 (1102 pcm) was able to maintain the commonly cited SDM value of ∼1000 pcm while HfB 2 (1002 pcm), Hf (984 pcm), and B 4 C (903 pcm) were able to marginally perform to that range considering uncertainties and practical constraints. This is a comprehensive neutronic feasibility and screening study. A full accident tolerance performance assessment (high-temperature oxidation, irradiation swelling and helium gas release, etc.) is out of the scope of this work. The materials highlighted here are presented and discussed as priority candidates for further investigation.

abstract: Improved Optical-fiber VErification System (IOVES) inherently includes superposed signals from adjacent bundles and exhibit on-site variability. This study proposes an automated defect-identification framework that combines Monte Carlo–simulated radiation profiles with a deep-learning model and a dynamic time warping (DTW) alignment procedure for robust field deployment. A simulation dataset representing normal and missing-bundle conditions was constructed, and an LSTM–Cross Attention model was designed to jointly leverage depth-dependent profiles and bundle-level source-term embeddings. On 333,640 validation labels, the model achieved an AUC of 0.9990 and an F1-score of 0.9969 under class imbalance, with a missing-bundle specificity of 0.9611. For field application, IOVES profiles acquired at the Wolsong CANDU spent fuel wet storage facility were preprocessed and aligned to simulation profiles via DTW. After correction, mean RMSE decreased by 51.88% and mean Pearson correlation increased to 0.9647, indicating improved structural agreement. Using DTW-corrected field inputs, the model classified all tested on-site positions as normal. Overall, the framework demonstrates that domain discrepancies between simulation and field measurements can be mitigated through algorithmic alignment and AI model, enabling scalable automated gross-defect verification for nuclear safeguards inspections.

A dynamically-truncated integral transport matrix low-order method for solving neutral particle transport problems
abstract: We develop a new low-order method for solving neutral particle transport problems, namely the Low-order Integral Transport Matrix Method (LITMM), and verify that the method can efficiently generate solutions akin to high-order S N transport operators. At this proof-of-principle stage, we used the Arbitrarily High Order Transport method of the Nodal type with 0th order local expansions (AHOT-N0) in 2-D Cartesian coordinates as the spatial discretization method in the derivation and in the numerical tests. Nevertheless, the method is applicable to any high-order method and can be implemented in production-level neutron transport codes. The low-order method is based on truncating elements of the integral transport matrix (ITM) below a user-specified threshold. The truncation process eliminates more elements as the optical thickness of the cells increases, resulting in a sparse ITM, denoted as the low-order operator, LITM. In this work, we develop a dynamic truncation algorithm that reduces the computational cost of assembling the LITM compared with constructing the full ITM and then truncating. We employed the Biconjugate Gradient Stabilized (BiCGSTAB) and Arnoldi iterations to solve fixed-source and eigenvalue problems. We tested LITMM in fixed-source configurations and for criticality benchmark problems by comparing the accuracy of LITMM’s results against high-order-operator solutions. We also evaluated LITMM’s computational performance against a matrix-free Krylov iterative method. The comparisons revealed that the low-order method is feasible and yields solutions comparable to those of their high-order operator counterparts, with remarkable computational efficiency, especially for the considered eigenvalue problems.

abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of regression techniques for modeling few-group cross-section libraries as a function of state parameters, with prediction targets that include both mean values and covariance matrices to represent aleatoric uncertainty from nuclear data perturbations. Beyond absolute accuracy, the primary focus is convergence performance: whether the prediction error decreases monotonically as the number of unique training samples Nbranch increases. The results show that the convergence behavior differs substantially across the methods. In particular, the transformed neural network model exhibits inconsistent, nonmonotonic convergence with respect to Nbranch, indicating limited robustness. In contrast, the transformed polynomial regression (tp-PR) model shows stable convergence and achieves the best performance at the largest training set (Nbranch = 1024) with a kinf error of 0.015%. A comparison of the predicted and reference keff distributions further shows that the tp-PR model was able to reproduce uncertainty induced by nuclear data uncertainty.

title: Impacts of long-term changes in materials of disposal canister and engineered barrier on underground criticality after disposal of spent nuclear fuel
abstract: In the present study, we conducted criticality analysis using a model that incorporates material changes occurring in disposal environments. The goal was to evaluate post-closure criticality of engineered barrier system for direct disposal of spent nuclear fuels with reasonable conservatism of material changes, avoiding excessive margins. The analyzed material changes included corrosion of fuel cladding, IT/GT tube (an Instrumentation Tube and a control rod Guide Tube), canister, and the resulting evolution of buffer materials. The reactivity was evaluated for those individual material changes and maximum reactivity was also evaluated considering the combination of their effects. The results show that the effective multiplication factor keff remained below the upper subcritical limit of 0.95 and was lower than the keff calculated by the previous conservative model. This result suggests that introducing realistic material changes, including those that potentially cause higher reactivity in geological environments, reduces the predicted likelihood of criticality when compared against the purely conservative model.

title: Multidimensional affective orientations and nuclear energy acceptance: integrating self- and threat-oriented negative affect and affective disengagement into the risk perception paradigm
abstract: Public acceptance of nuclear energy has traditionally been explained through the risk perception paradigm, which emphasizes cognitive evaluations of risks, benefits, trust, and knowledge. Yet emotional responses remain conceptually under-specified and frequently operationalized as undifferentiated negative affect. This study advances a multidimensional framework of affective orientation by distinguishing among self-oriented negative affect, threat-oriented negative affect, and affective disengagement. Self-oriented negative affect, measured through guilt and depression, is interpreted cautiously as inwardly directed affect that may involve moral burden, responsibility attribution, or perceived helplessness rather than direct emotion toward nuclear technology alone. Drawing on survey data from 1,970 Korean adults collected in June-July 2025, we examine how these affective orientations shape both personal acceptance (willingness to bear local exposure) and social acceptance (support for national nuclear policy). Hierarchical regression and interaction analyses show that emotional differentiation improves explanatory precision beyond conventional cognitive predictors. Threat-oriented negative affect consistently reduces both personal and social acceptance, self-oriented negative affect is positively associated with personal – but not social – acceptance, and affective disengagement facilitates passive social acceptance while exhibiting limited influence on personal acceptance. These findings demonstrate that emotions do not operate as a uniform barrier to nuclear energy. Instead, affective orientations shape technological acceptance through distinct functional pathways and by structuring the cognitive processing of risk information. Incorporating emotional heterogeneity into the risk perception paradigm offers a more precise theoretical account of energy technology acceptance and suggests that policy communication strategies should be calibrated to specific emotional profiles rather than relying solely on technical risk information.

Comprehensive thermodynamic screening of low-GWP refrigerant mixtures for micro-scale vapour compression refrigerators and heat pumps
abstract: As the demand for high-performance micro and power electronics grows, micro-scale vapour compression refrigeration (VCR) systems and heat pumps (VCHP) have emerged as critical technologies for active heating and cooling. However, the progressive phase-down of hydrofluorocarbon refrigerants under international environmental regulations, necessitates the identification of low-global warming potential alternatives specifically optimized for the unique constraints of small-scale hardware, such as limited compressor displacement and low refrigerant charge. This study presents a comprehensive and systematic thermodynamic screening of approximately 30,000 refrigerant compositions, including pure fluids, binary, and ternary mixtures, specifically aimed at three key application scenarios: domestic and commercial micro-appliances, personal cooling systems for hostile environments, and reversible heat pumps for electric vehicle cabin and battery management. Using a multi-criteria decision-making approach based on the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method to maximize simultaneously coefficient of performance and volumetric heating and cooling capacity, optimal candidates were identified across four practical scenarios: high-performance, safety-critical – low-flammability (A1), low-pressure, and a combined low-pressure/non-flammable scenario. Findings demonstrate that added complexity in ternary mixtures offer no significant thermodynamic advantage over simpler binary blends for micro-scale applications. Final recommendations for next-generation micro-VCR/VCHP systems include: R1270 and R290/RE170 (60/40)% for maximum performance; R1234yf/R1224yd(Z) (72/28)% for safety-critical (A1) applications; RE170/R600 (65/35)% and R600/R1270 (28/72)% for natural, low-pressure operation; and R1234ze(E)/R1233zd(E) (72/28)% or R1234ze(E)/R1224yd(Z) (68/32)% for combined constraints. This study establishes a structured roadmap to navigate the complex landscape of sustainable refrigerant selection in the micro-VCR/VCHP domain.

abstract: The growing interest in targeted alpha therapy has highlighted the need for stable and efficient production methods for multiple alpha-emitting nuclides. This study investigates an efficient method for producing 228Th, a parent nuclide for 212Pb generator, via multiple neutron capture reactions using 226Ra as the target nuclide under spectrum-tailored irradiation in a fast reactor. By installing moderators into the radial reflector region, the effects of moderator materials, moderator volume fraction, and stepwise irradiation schemes on the transmutation pathway from 226Ra to 228Th were systematically evaluated. The results indicate that irradiation of a 1-g 226Ra target for four cycles using a beryllium moderator at a 100% volume fraction, which is optimal for the 226Ra (n,γ) reaction, followed by one cycle using a ZrH1.65 moderator at a 50% volume fraction, which is optimal for the 227Ac (n,γ) reaction, enables annual production of approximately 37 Ci of 228Th per gram of 226Ra. This activity corresponds to the 228Th inventory after five irradiation cycles and includes radioactive decay during irradiation and cooling periods.

title: Study on the separation performance of polyimide hollow fiber membranes for radon and oxygen
abstract: ABSTRACT As a naturally occurring radioactive inert gas, radon poses a significant risk of lung cancer upon long-term exposure. To address the limitations of conventional radon mitigation methods (ventilation, coating/sealing, and adsorption), such as high energy consumption, material aging, and limited processing capacity, this study innovatively introduces polyimide hollow fiber membranes into the field of radon gas separation. By systematically investigating the effects of transmembrane pressure difference (100-500 kPa), flow ratio (1:1, 1:2, 2:1) and permeate-side pressures (0-400 kPa) on Rn-O 2 separation performance and mass transfer mechanisms, oxygen recovery rate and radon transmission rate were proposed as key evaluation metrics. The results show that: 1) Oxygen recovery increases with both Δ P and the flow ratio, reaching a maximum (>95%) at Δ P =500 kPa and Q K / Q M =2:1. However, under constant transmembrane pressure conditions, an increase in permeate-side pressure suppresses oxygen recovery efficiency. 2) Radon transmission is predominantly governed by the flow ratio, while Δ P and P K exert only marginal effects. The lowest radon transmission rate of 25.6-28.2% is achieved at a flow ratio of 1:2. This study first reports the differential mass transfer of radon–oxygen in hollow fiber membranes, offering theoretical and experimental support for radioactive gas separation membrane technology.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of Simulation Parameters for Gas-Liquid Two-Phase Flow in a Hooked Corrugated Plate Separator
abstract: Corrugated plate gas–liquid separators are widely used, but CFD models for their design often lack systematic evaluation of key numerical settings. This study performs three-dimensional simulations of a single-hook corrugated plate to assess mesh requirements, turbulence closure, interphase coupling, droplet force terms, and turbulent dispersion models. The results indicate that a boundary-layer growth rate of 1.1, at least 15 prism layers, and y + ≤ 0.2 provide the best compromise between accuracy and cost. The Realizable k–ε model with enhanced wall functions outperforms the SST k–ω model in predicting pressure drop and separation efficiency. For droplets much smaller than the characteristic flow scale, a one-way coupling strategy is sufficient and improves computational efficiency. Including drag, virtual mass, and pressure-gradient forces yields the highest accuracy, whereas activating virtual mass alone degrades predictions. Combining the Discrete Random Walk model with Random Eddy Lifetime best reproduces droplet dispersion and significantly improves agreement with experimental separation efficiencies. These findings provide practical modeling guidelines for reliable and efficient CFD design of corrugated plate separators.

Heat transfer characteristics of lead-bismuth eutectic and CO2-based mixtures in straight-channel printed circuit heat exchangers
abstract: Lead-cooled fast reactors coupled with supercritical CO 2 Brayton cycles represent a highly promising energy conversion technology for next generation nuclear power system. The overall thermal performance of these systems can be further enhanced by introducing CO 2 -based mixtures, however, investigations on the heat transfer and flow characteristics of lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) and CO 2 -based mixtures in the intermediate heat exchanger between the primary and secondary loops remain scarce. In this work, numerical simulations were conducted to investigate the heat transfer and flow characteristics of LBE and CO 2 -based mixtures in straight-channel printed circuit heat exchangers (PCHEs). The performance of CO 2 -propane, CO 2 -krypton and CO 2 -xenon at different mixing mole fractions was compared. The results show that, among the investigated CO 2 -based mixtures, the CO 2 -propane mixture provides the most favourable heat transfer performance when coupled with LBE. Compared with pure CO 2 under the same operating conditions, the overall heat transfer coefficient of the CO 2 -propane/LBE PCHE increases by up to 40%. In addition, the impact of key parameters ( e.g. , inlet velocity, mass flow rate, inlet temperature, and pressure) on the heat transfer characteristics of CO 2 -propane mixtures was analysed. Finally, correlations for the Nusselt number and friction factor were derived using the simulation results, with prediction errors within ±3% for CO 2 -propane mixtures with a propane mole fraction in the range of 0.05-0.30. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing and optimizing PCHEs with LBE and CO 2 -based mixtures serving as heat transfer media.

title: CO2 transpiration cooling for infrared-stealth thermal protection: An experimental and numerical study on mid-infrared radiation of a porous plate
Thermal Performance Characterization of a Miniature Loop Heat Pipe in Vacuum: Fixed and Variable Conductance Modes of Operation
abstract: This study presents an experimental investigation of a miniature loop heat pipe operating inside a thermal vacuum chamber, providing novel insights into its behavior under vacuum conditions with a focus on fixed versus variable conductance modes of operation. Results demonstrate that, unlike in ambient conditions where variable conductance mode is typically observed, the miniature loop heat pipe operates exclusively in the fixed conductance mode under vacuum. This is due to the absence of convective heat exchange between the liquid line and the surroundings, which is critical for autonomous temperature regulation. The experiments systematically evaluate the effects of sink temperature (−10 °C to 35 °C) and heat load variations (up to 120 W) on thermal performance, revealing that thermal resistance decreases with lower sink temperatures, ranging from 0.10 to 0.20 K/W. Additionally, the evaporator heat transfer coefficient stabilizes at higher heat loads, peaking at 4 kW/(m2·K) for a 0 °C sink. These findings advance the understanding of miniature loop heat pipe behavior in vacuum environments, supporting the development of reliable thermal control systems for space applications. Numerical parametric analyses conducted with the model indicate that enlarging the vapor line diameter and increasing wick porosity enhance thermal performance by decreasing pressure drops.

title: Flow Boiling Characteristics of Water–Al 2 O 3 and R134a-Al 2 O 3 in Multi-layered Wavy Microchannels
abstract: This study presents a numerical investigation of flow boiling in multilayered wavy microchannels using nanofluids to enhance thermo-hydraulic performance. A coupled volume of fluid-Lee phase change method and Discrete Phase Model are employed to capture complex vapor-liquid interfaces and nanoparticle dynamics. Water–aluminum oxide and R134a-aluminum oxide are examined at various volumetric concentrations, mass fluxes, and heat fluxes. Unlike prior studies on straight channels, this work investigates wavy geometries to reveal heat transfer enhancements. An artificial neural network is trained to predict Nusselt number and friction factor ratios, and predictions are optimized using a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm. Results indicate that double-layered wavy microchannels outperform single-layer configurations, achieving a maximum Nusselt number of 16 and a performance factor of 1.406. Water–aluminum oxide exhibits higher heat transfer coefficients, while the refrigerant mixture offers lower pressure drop. The machine learning model predicts results with minimal deviation from simulations, identifying an optimal solution with a performance factor of 1.422. This work offers new insights into the synergy between microchannel geometry, nanofluid properties, and data-driven optimization.
